item.title: What Are We Celebrating? The Four Faces of Hanukah | Hilchot Hanukah | Siman 670
item.description:
The first shiur of the course opens Hilchot Hanukah with Siman 670. What are we really celebrating? The four aspects of Hanukah (the military victory, the oil, Yehudit, and the re-inauguration of the altar) and how every custom maps onto them; why eulogies and fasting are forbidden and what that means today; the women's custom not to work while the lights burn; whether Hanukah parties are a mitzvah, and why Purim has a feast but Hanukah doesn't; and the opening of Siman 671: three levels of lighting, and why Sephardim light one menorah per household.
Part 1 of 7 in Dayan Kada's Thursday Night Halacha series on Hilchot Hanukah (Shulhan Arukh, Orah Hayim 670–684), given in November 2024.

item.title: Where to Place the Menorah: Doorway, Window or Table? | Hilchot Hanukah | Siman 671
item.description:
Siman 671: where the menorah should stand. Two wicks and the problem of a 'bonfire' (and why menorahs are never round); outside, the window, inside the door or the table; where the shamash really comes from; the minimum and maximum heights; why lighting makes the mitzvah, so you can't light by a bedside and then move it; mezuzah on the right, menorah on the left; and what to do in a flat above twenty amot.
Part 2 of 7 in Dayan Kada's Thursday Night Halacha series on Hilchot Hanukah (Shulhan Arukh, Orah Hayim 670–684), given in November 2024.

item.title: A Blessing on a Custom? The Shul Menorah & When to Light | Hilchot Hanukah | Siman 671–672
item.description:
The synagogue menorah: a custom unknown to the Talmud and the Rambam, its five reasons, and how we can say a berachah on a custom at all. Public menorahs at weddings and shopping centres, who counts toward the ten, Sheheḥeyanu after lighting in shul, a house with two entrances, and the earliest time to light, with why you shouldn't wait for the calendar's Shabbat-ends time.
Part 3 of 7 in Dayan Kada's Thursday Night Halacha series on Hilchot Hanukah (Shulhan Arukh, Orah Hayim 670–684), given in November 2024.

item.title: When to Light, How Late, and Which Oils: Timing & Fuel | Hilchot Hanukah | Siman 672–673
item.description:
Simanim 672–673: Arvit or the menorah first; lighting from pelag haminḥah; how late you may still light, even alone with everyone asleep; whether the family should wait for a spouse coming home late; why you may (and should) put the menorah out when you go out; which oils and wicks are best and why we skip Bameh Madlikin on Shabbat Hanukah; the shamash, and what happens if a light goes out.
Part 4 of 7 in Dayan Kada's Thursday Night Halacha series on Hilchot Hanukah (Shulhan Arukh, Orah Hayim 670–684), given in November 2024.

item.title: One Flame From Another & Who May Light | Hilchot Hanukah | Siman 674–676
item.description:
Simanim 674–676: lighting one Hanukah light from another (one of only three places Shmuel beats Rav on an issur), the lighting not the placing makes the mitzvah, and who may light: women, children of ḥinuch age (and the Syrian custom), a blind person, a ḥeresh and a convert; plus the text of the berachot, 'ner Ḥanukah' or 'ner shel Ḥanukah'.
Part 5 of 7 in Dayan Kada's Thursday Night Halacha series on Hilchot Hanukah (Shulhan Arukh, Orah Hayim 670–684), given in December 2024.

item.title: Blessings, Which Way to Light & Hanukah Meets Shabbat | Hilchot Hanukah | Siman 676–681
item.description:
Simanim 676–681: the berachot and Sheheḥeyanu, the berachah on seeing a menorah, Hanerot Hallalu, and which way to light; Shabbat candles vs. Hanukah lights vs. Kiddush when money is short; Hanukah or Shabbat candles first on Friday; protecting the lights from the door; and Havdalah or the menorah first on Motza'ei Shabbat.
